title: Tell me about a time you delivered under an aggressive deadline
prompt: Tell me about a time you faced a tight deadline for something important. Explain how you prioritized, communicated the limits and decided what could be delivered safely. An honest decision to change scope or escalate an unrealistic deadline can be a strong example.
blurb: Tight deadline: did they prioritize and make smart, honest tradeoffs — or just heroics and hidden debt?

rubric.label: Situation & the deadline
rubric.description: Explains the deliverable, time constraint and why timing mattered in that setting.

rubric.label: Owning delivery
rubric.description: Explains their role in planning, prioritizing, clarifying expectations or escalating an unrealistic commitment.

rubric.label: Specific contribution and decisions
rubric.description: Describes specific tradeoffs involving scope, sequencing, help or timing while preserving required safety and quality.

rubric.label: Outcome and evidence
rubric.description: Reports what was delivered, deferred or missed and any effects using supported qualitative or quantitative evidence; meeting the date at any cost is not required.

rubric.label: Reflection & sustainability
rubric.description: Explains a realistic improvement to planning or communication and considers sustainable workload rather than rewarding unpaid or excessive hours.

rubric.label: Clear, relevant communication
rubric.description: Explains how they communicated a material limit, change or risk to the people affected. Assess meaning and relevant evidence, not accent, emotional tone or a prescribed story order.

reference.scenario: Explore planning under a tight deadline in any relevant responsibility. Assess realistic priorities, explicit tradeoffs, communication and safety. The candidate may have changed scope, sought help or escalated the deadline; completing everything or working excessive hours is not the success criterion.
model_points: Clarifies what was needed, by when and what was known about available capacity.
Identifies the candidate’s planning or communication contribution.
Protects required safety and quality while choosing a feasible scope or explaining that it is not feasible.
Communicates a material change, risk or decision through a suitable channel.
Describes actual delivery and any remaining work honestly without requiring monetary or numeric impact.
Identifies a concrete way to reduce future avoidable pressure or make tradeoffs visible earlier.

probes.question: What choices did you make about the work itself?

probes.trigger: candidate promises full scope despite a stated capacity problem
probes.question: What made that plan feasible?
How did you communicate the change?

red_flags: Hides a known delivery or safety risk from people who need it to make a decision.
Treats unpaid or excessive hours as the required proof of commitment.
Claims completion while acknowledging that essential checks or agreed work remain undone.
follow_ups: What did you decide to defer or escalate?
What would make a similar deadline more realistic next time?
reference.exemplar_answer: Illustrative example only; it is not a required setting, answer order or achievement standard. Before a community workshop, our team had less preparation time than expected. I checked which materials were essential and proposed dropping an optional display so we could finish the participant instructions and safety checks. I told the organizer what would be ready and what would be absent. The workshop went ahead with a smaller setup. Next time I would confirm the essential materials earlier instead of treating every idea as a requirement.
reference.assessment_contract: Assess the selected competency from concrete job-relevant evidence. Examples from paid work, study, volunteering, caregiving, informal work, military service and community activities are equally eligible when relevant. A modest example is sufficient if it shows the competency; employer prestige, formal title and financial scale are not criteria. Accept qualitative or quantitative outcomes supported by the account, including partial or unsuccessful outcomes. Do not require a numeric metric, STAR order, particular pronouns, composure, enthusiasm or a particular communication style. Identify personal contribution by meaning while preserving credit to others. Assess intelligibility and relevance, not accent, fluency, verbosity, visible emotion, disability or private circumstances. Mark genuinely missing evidence not assessed; do not infer poor competence or dishonesty from an absent example. A clearly labeled hypothetical may be discussed as situational practice but must not count as demonstrated past experience. Respect scope of practice, authorization, safety and ethical duties; pausing, declining, reporting or escalating can be sound judgment. Never require obedience, direct confrontation, unpaid overwork or successful persuasion regardless of the circumstances.
